lesson_title: A Town as Big as Cape Town
hook_text: In 1801, travellers reached a town north of the Orange River and estimated it was as big as Cape Town. Most people have never heard of it.
clip_script: Dithakong, capital of the Batlhaping: thousands of homes in neat wards, a central kgotla where men debated, fields of sorghum, cattle posts on the horizon. The Batswana were master craftspeople: iron hoes and spears, copper beads, and fur karosses stitched so finely they were prized in Cape Town. On their southern borders, they traded ivory, hides, skins and metalwork with Kora and Griqua traders for glass beads, tobacco, cloth and, later, guns. That trade brought wealth, missionaries, and more elephant hunting than ever before.
visual_style: An aerial reconstruction of a large Tswana town with circular wards; close-ups of a fur kaross, copper beads and an iron hoe; a trading scene with wagons.
pacing: A reveal, a tour of crafts, a trade montage, a cautionary close.
